strings: Coming from Glapp? Bring the history with you
If you can get a CSV of your Glapp data, Dozify can read it. You see how many records it found, and which columns it read, before anything is written. Free, and Dozify does not upload the file.
The columns Dozify looks for in a Glapp CSV

Not every format has been tested with a real export; the preview shows what was read before anything is written. Open your CSV and compare the header row. Dozify matches a column by any of these names, and it does not mind capitalisation or a unit written in brackets. Anything it cannot place is listed on the preview screen by name, so you can see what was left out rather than wondering.
If your dose column is headed “units”

Those rows are listed for you instead of being converted. A unit is a volume on a syringe, and how many milligrams sit in it depends on the concentration of your vial — a number the file does not carry. Writing them into a milligram field would record the wrong dose without anything downstream questioning it, so Dozify lists them as skipped; you can log those doses by hand in the amount your prescriber uses. Why there is no one conversion →

Dozify is a tracking tool, not a medical device. It does not recommend doses and does not provide medical advice.
